articleBlocks: I first thought that the clues might be pointing to a type of fancy pastry, but that theory broke when I realized that not all of these desserts are typically considered pastries.
The clue 'Seven-layer cake' made me realize that all the desserts have multiple layers, which was a turning point in my solve.
I considered the possibility that the category might be European desserts, but that didn't quite fit because not all of these desserts are exclusively European.
As I looked closer at the clues, I realized that each one was a type of dessert that is specifically known for having multiple layers.
The full set of clues confirms a specific category of desserts that all have multiple layers, which is a more precise fit than the nearby wrong reads.
Trifle, for example, is a traditional English dessert made with layers of sponge cake, fruit, and custard.
Parfait is a French dessert made with layers of cream, sugar, and fruit.
Tiramisu is an Italian dessert made with layers of ladyfingers, mascarpone cheese, and espresso.
Baklava is a Middle Eastern pastry made with layers of phyllo dough, nuts, and honey.
Seven-layer cake is a type of cake that is made with seven layers of cake and frosting.
In hindsight, the connection between the clues is clear: all of these desserts have multiple layers, which is a distinctive characteristic.
The puzzle requires a closer look to realize the connection between the clues, but the answer is satisfyingly precise once you see it.
solutionNarrative: I first read Trifle and Parfait as just dessert names and drifted toward fancy cakes. That was too narrow because the full board is not only cakes.
Seven-layer cake changed the direction because it made the layer idea impossible to ignore.
I then checked the rest: trifle, parfait, tiramisu, and baklava are all desserts known for layers.

That left very little room for the earlier false start. The answer was "Desserts (all with many layers)", and the last step was simply making sure every clue used that same reading cleanly before treating the solve as finished.
